title: The Porter's Son (The Triumph of Art)

full_text:
Little George was the son of the general's basement gatekeeper. In the grand salon above lived the general's lovely daughter, Emily. The proud general mocked George when the boy sketched figures on wrapping paper: "A porter's son belongs with brooms, not brushes!"

George persevered. He worked by day, studied classical drawing by night, and won the gold medal of the Royal Academy in Rome!

Years later, George returned as the renowned master architect who designed the imperial museum. When the general's family faced bankruptcy, George quietly bought their mortgage, restored their honor, and married his childhood friend Emily, proving that true nobility resides in the genius of the soul.
moral: True talent and hard work will always triumph over social snobbery and inherited privilege.
